_what: Invariant 10's ceiling, per frame directory: how many DOMAIN WORDS each may carry outside comments, counted by splitting identifiers into words. A ratchet — these numbers may fall and may not rise. Written by reading each one, never seeded blind (B-100).
_vocabulary: Two derived halves, never a hand-kept list. The nine feature directory names, from the tree: account, acquisition, arrivals, library, maintenance, media, releases, settings, system. AND the seven page aliases, parsed from lib/addresses.ts: acq, arr, cfg, lib, maint, profile, sys. The aliases were the missing half — the frame does not write `acquisition`, it writes `acq`, and app/page-host.tsx IS a table keyed by them.
_measured: 2026-08-29, by scripts/check-frame-domain.py. Three earlier readings were wrong and each was found by a mutation or a reviewer, never by re-reading the number: `\bword\b` read 53 in app/ where there are 124, because a domain word reaches the frame INSIDE an identifier; the aliases above were invisible entirely; and a module specifier was counted as an identifier, which is what put `lib` twice into a directory whose ceiling is ZERO. Re-measured 2026-08-30 at L15 phase 1, per file, by this script's own reader (`count_directory`) rather than by re-reading the printed total.

ui._why: ZERO, and it is true. `ui/` is the component vocabulary and names no subject. Its only two hits were the paths `../lib/store-access` and `../../lib/engine-drawing` — the FRAME's own lib/ directory, a word that collides with the library page's alias and means the opposite thing. A file path is not a name the code chose, so specifiers are no longer read and the count is a real zero.

lib._why: ALL SIXTEEN are in `lib/queue.ts` — the staging and acquisition queue, shared by two features, and invariant 7 is absolute so a queue both read had nowhere else to go. No other file in lib/ carries one. § 3 calls that « not one reviewed line » and hands the arbitration (a `domain/` bucket of its own) to a later wave. `lib/addresses.ts` is exempt by the invariant itself — an address IS the page's identity — and it is the ONLY exemption: `lib/engine-drawing.ts` stood here too and the invariant does not name it, so it is counted now and carries none. **RAISED TO 18 AT L11**, and it is the « one reviewed line » the invariant blesses rather than a drift: `ADDRESSES_THAT_MOVE_TOGETHER` names the two addresses THIS module's own optimistic write spans — `takeOutOfQueue` removes the card from whichever of the two lists holds it, and every online path here already invalidates both. A replay out of the offline queue has to do the same, and the pairing was first written in `app/outbox-wiring.ts`, where this guard correctly refused it: those are domain addresses and the frame may not name them. It belongs where the two-key write is MADE. The frame reads the list without knowing what is in it. It falls again with the rest of this file when the `domain/` bucket § 3 defers arrives — L16 brings its second member.

app._why: The frame naming its PAGES, which is the exception the invariant blesses BY NAME — « whatever table the shell reads to compose navigation ». L15 made that table exist ONCE (`app/navigation.ts`, 48) where it existed four times, and the arithmetic is the whole justification: 98 − 26 (page-host.tsx, which carried the id→component list and now carries none) + 48 (the one table: id, path, component, label key, icon, group, bar, action button and badge, per page) + 1 (`app/icons.ts`, whose `library` is a drawing's name) = 121, and +7 at phase 7 for `app/drawer.tsx` (the drawer draws the same table's rows, grouped) = 128, and +1 at phase 13 for `app/entry.ts` (the sign-in gate composes the address of the page it lets through) = 129. Read file by file at phase 1: navigation.ts 48, reference.d.ts 18, router-tree.tsx 18, live-updates.ts 12, history-bridge.ts 8, engine-data.ts 7, shell.tsx 6, not-found.tsx 2, icons.ts 1, store.ts 1. The first is the table the invariant names; the next two are the list of routes and the engine seam's type slice, which every framework has somewhere; live-updates.ts is one import per feature (D-L10-1). LOWER IT WHEN THE ENGINE GOES: engine-data.ts (7) and reference.d.ts (18) die with it, and a ceiling nobody lowers becomes room for a defect nobody notices. **LOWERED TO 126 AT L19 phase 03**, and it is the sentence above being acted on rather than deferred: `engine-data.ts` loses a family every time a producer moves into its feature and declares what it needs beside itself, so it fell from 7 to 4 when `MAINT_ACTIONS` left. It is lowered in the commit that moves the producer, because a ceiling lowered later is a ceiling nobody compared.
